subject: health
unitTitle: Navigating Health Systems, Coverage, and Confidentiality
title: Application or project: preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question
focus: preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question
essentialQuestion: How does a person actually get care, and what does it cost them to try?
materials: course-supplied fictional coverage summaries and case files
keyPoints: Appointment preparation uses a concise concern, timeline, current medicines if relevant, questions, and a next-step summary; a fictional case can practice the skill privately.
Compare care options by function, access, safety, and sustainability; avoid appearance rules, shame, rigid perfection, or assumptions about another person’s habits.

For preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Run three fictional cases through the system: choose the right level of care, estimate the cost path, prepare the questions, and identify the confidentiality rule that applies.
studentTask: Use the supplied fictional day to create a care plan for preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question. Identify two needs or barriers, choose two feasible supports, and explain how each supports function or recovery without appearance rules, shame, or a requirement to reveal personal habits.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Walkthroughs may be written, charted, narrated, or completed on a supplied decision frame with vocabulary pre-defined.
extensionChallenge: Apply preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
Walkthroughs may be written, charted, narrated, or completed on a supplied decision frame with vocabulary pre-defined.
trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Explain preparing for an appointment and asking a clinician a real question accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
